publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
abstract: Increasing kernel weight is an effective way for improving grain-yield in wheat. Identification of major QTLs for kernel weight without negative effects on other yield-related traits is important to continuous yield improvement. We developed a population of F6 recombinant inbred lines (RILs) from Jimai120 x Jimai325 and identified eight QTLs for thousand-kernel weight (TKW), kernel length (KL) and kernel width (KW) in five environments. One QTL on chromosome arm 3DL consistently showed major effects on TKW (QTkw.cau-3DL) and KL in five field experiments, accounting for up to 16.43% and 13.87% of phenotypic variation, respectively. QTkw.cau-3DL was confined to a 5.72 Mb (3.48 cM) interval between 554.39 and 560.11 Mb. This QTL was validated in a pair of near-isogenic lines (NILs) and in a new double haploid (DH) population. QTkw.cau-3DL increased kernel weight per spike (KWPS) without any negative effect on heading data (HD), plant height (PH), spike length (SL), spikelet number per spike (SNS) and kernels number per spike (KNPS). It increased 6.2% of grain yield under regular field production conditions. Analyses on its marker haplotype and geographical distribution in a nationwide collection of 630 Chinese wheat cultivars and breeding lines showed that QTkw.cau-3DL has not been widely deployed in Chinese wheat breeding programs. QTkw.cau-3DL is a novel QTL for increasing TKW through increasing KL, therefore, it is an important locus for enhancing wheat grain yield. The tightly linked user-friendly markers developed in this study should facilitate map-based cloning and marker-assisted selection of the QTL in wheat breeding programs.
title: Mapping and validation of a major QTL, QTkw.cau-3DL, controls kernel weight by regulating kernel length in wheat
